item.title: Leaked EU paper envisions dumping migrant sea rescues onto non-European states
item.description: The EU has been mulling sending people rescued in the Mediterranean directly to coastal states outside of Europe, according to an internal EU document.

item.title: 73 days to election: Roma people are for ‘cleaning shit-filled toilets’, says Hungarian minister
item.description: Our ongoing week-by-week debrief by award-winning journalist Veronika Munk, explaining the most important political developments in Hungary in the run-up to the crunch April election.

item.title: Far-right MEP tries to silence EUobserver over election-monitoring ban
item.description: French far-right MEP Virginie Joron claimed she was never punished for rogue election monitoring, but the EU Parliament confirmed she was lying, amid a wider crackdown.

item.title: The EU-India trade deal: ‘mother of deals’ or ‘overhyped’ and full of loopholes? The answer may be both
item.description: Why the EU-India trade deal sparks both praise and pushback — explained.

item.title: Iran ‘terrorist’ label does not signify backing for US strikes, EU says
item.description: Europe's designation of Iran's main army branch as “terrorists” on Thursday is not an endorsement of US military strikes, the EU's top diplomat has said.

item.title: Made in India, or Made in Heaven? Winners and losers in this week’s EU-India deal
item.description: A former EU trade negotiator reflects on the winners and losers in the new EU-India deal. The big question is whether this agreement signifies a tectonic shift in world trade: the world’s two biggest democracies, the second and fourth largest economies, asserting common values in the face of a rogue US and a hostile China? The EU certainly likes to think so.

item.title: Listen: Can we, Europeans, do something to stop the bloodshed in Iran?
item.description: The EU has just decided to tag the Islamic Revolutionary Guards as a terrorist organisation. What does that actually mean?

item.title: EU backs Morocco’s plan for Western Sahara, as Brussels edges closer to Rabat
item.description: The autonomy plan, backed by Brussels, would mean local legislative, executive and judicial authorities for Western Sahara elected by its residents, while Rabat would control its sovereignty, as well as defence, foreign affairs and religious affairs

item.title: Behind EU’s December asylum relocation pledges: More deal-making, fewer transfers
item.description: Most commitments made by EU states in December to receive asylum seekers arriving primarily in Italy and Greece are actually alternative forms of support.

item.title: Five ways the EU has already appeased Trump
item.description: Donald Trump has been back in White House for just over a year, and EU has struggled to balance safeguarding its own economic and social interests while maintaining a US relationship it needs to its security. Here are five ways the EU is adjusting to — many would say appeasing — Trump’s agenda.
